notes: Libretto by Lorenzo Da Ponte (1786); words follow the engraving’s spelling (e.g. dira without accent, Èver as printed). IPA as sung, stressed syllable marked; translation literal, for meaning.

phrases.translation: I know.
Here comes the march,
let us go!

phrases.original: ai vostri posti, o belle, ai vostri posti!
phrases.translation: to your places, my beauties, to your places!
phrases.ipa: ai ˈvɔs.tri ˈpo.sti o ˈbɛl.le ai ˈvɔs.tri ˈpo.sti

phrases.translation: Susanna, give me your arm!
Here it is!
Insolent pair!
I am frozen!
Countess!
Let us not speak now.

phrases.original: Ecco quì le due nozze, riceverle dobbiam,
phrases.translation: Here are the two weddings; we must receive them,
phrases.ipa: ˈɛk.ko ˈkwi le ˈdu.e ˈnɔt.tse ri.tʃeˈver.le dobˈbjam

phrases.original: alfin si tratta d'una vostra protetta.
phrases.translation: after all, it concerns a protégée of yours.
phrases.ipa: alˈfin si ˈtrat.ta ˈdu.na ˈvɔ.stra proˈtɛt.ta

phrases.translation: Let us sit down!
Let us sit down!
and plan revenge.
Faithful lovers, followers of honour,
sing, praise so wise a lord.

phrases.translation: Ha! ha!
I see the game.
A love letter that some gallant
gave him in passing,
and it was sealed with a pin,

phrases.original: ond' egli si punse il dito,

phrases.translation: Go, my friends!
